svg.text: S1 — API 5xx from database I/O saturation (gp2 burst-balance / IOPS ceiling)

The slow-burn cause hidden behind an application symptom. Mechanism from AWS RDS metric definitions (READ); timeline shape from Honeycomb 2023, GitLab 2026, Grafana Labs — no first-party postmortem names BurstBalance with minutes; say so.
nobody alerts on a leading indicator
synthetic / SLO alert, not the cause metric
H2 single bad query / plan flip
H3 lock queue · H4 connection storm
H4 ✗ ordering: IO first · H5 n/a class
is IO latency up with balance > 20%? no
cause: gp2 credits exhausted on db-main
red herring named: CPU looked hot (Chen)

Discriminating queries: CloudWatch BurstBalance · EBSIOBalance% · ReadIOPS/WriteIOPS · ReadLatency · DiskQueueDepth · DatabaseConnections · CPUCreditBalance ‖ SQL: pg_stat_activity wait_event grouping · pg_stat_statements by total_exec_time · pg_locks NOT granted ‖ PromQL: 5xx ratio · p99 · hikaricp_connections_pending.

Grounding: AWS RDS metric reference (READ) · Honeycomb ‘RDS clogs & cache-refresh crash loops’ 2023, 68 min (READ) · GitLab INC 2026-08-27 plan flip → 500s, fixed by ANALYZE (READ) · Grafana Labs unbounded join, 28 min human vs 8 min assistant (READ) · Chen RDS gp2 burst post 2025 (INFERRED, page blocked).

Open: no first-party postmortem names BurstBalance with a minute timeline — next probe is GitLab gl-infra ‘disk util|iops’ and SRE Weekly ‘burst balance’. Why it matters to Smokejumper: none of the four surveyed products publishes an IOPS example; the leading indicator is the open lane.
